headings: Risk signals exist early. Today they stay fragmented.
paragraphs: Lifestyle, family history, vital signs, blood chemistry and tissue changes each tell part of the story, often years before symptoms. In routine care they are seen separately, if at all. A single test can look normal while the real pattern sits across several results.
Salt Lick's proprietary AI reads every signal together, cross-checks them and highlights the people who need attention first, so fewer people at risk are missed.

images.alt: Many health signals combining into one risk score

headings: Four layers of evidence in a single visit.
eyebrows: What a Salt Lick screening includes
paragraphs: A 60-second scan reads more than 20 vital signs from subtle changes in the skin, including heart rate, heart-rate variability, oxygen saturation, breathing rate, blood-pressure trends and stress indicators. No touch, no needle.
A compact analyser measures metabolic health and tumour markers associated with breast, lung, prostate, gastrointestinal and oral cancers, from a very small sample, with results in minutes.
Safe autofluorescent light reveals suspicious changes in the mouth that are hard to see with the naked eye. Quick, painless and suitable for repeat screening.
Optical transillumination uses light to reveal abnormal blood-vessel patterns, cysts and masses, with no X-rays and no compression. Performed in a private, women-only space.

headings: The same disease. A different moment. A different ending.

headings: Acting earlier saves lives and resources.
paragraphs: In India, treating cancer found early costs around INR 0.75 lakh per patient, compared with up to INR 10 lakh when found late.

Reducing new cancer cases by just 10% would spare around 160,000 people a year and save an estimated INR 4,800 crore (about USD 550 million) in treatment costs annually. Across the world, the opportunity is many times larger.
